knowledge:
- key_parameters: object=A SummarizedExperiment, DESeqDataSet, or count matrix containing transcript-level counts ;; metadata=A data frame containing sample metadata (required if object is a count matrix) ;; group_col=The column name in metadata specifying the comparison groups ;; sample_col=The column name in metadata specifying sample IDs ;; baseline=The name of the baseline/control group ;; case=The name of the case/condition group ;; experiment_title=A character string used to name stored intermediate results files ;; store_results=Logical indicating whether to save intermediate transcript-level results (recommended to set to TRUE) ;; use_limma=Logical indicating whether to use limma (eBayes and diffSplice) instead of DESeq2/DEXSeq ;; covariates=Character vector of metadata columns to include as covariates in the model ;; run_sva=Logical indicating whether to run Surrogate Variable Analysis (SVA) to account for batch effects
- alternatives: limma=Can be used instead of DESeq2/DEXSeq by setting use_limma = TRUE ;; IsoformSwitchAnalyzeR=Used for identifying and visualizing isoform switches with functional consequences, with built-in import/export functions to/from pairedGSEA ;; alternative_ora=Users can run their own gene set analysis methods directly on the diff_results output instead of using paired_ora
- when_to_use: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq data aligned to the transcript level and want to perform a unified, comparable analysis of both differential gene expression and differential splicing, followed by pathway enrichment.
- pitfalls: rownames_format=Rownames of the input count matrix or SummarizedExperiment must be formatted strictly as 'gene:transcript' ;; dgs_lfc_interpretation=DGS log2 fold changes are assigned to the log2 fold change of the transcript with the lowest p-value and should be interpreted with caution ;; execution_time=DEXSeq can take 20-30 minutes to run depending on data size and resources ;; sample_matching=Ensure all sample IDs in the count matrix columns match the sample_col values in the metadata exactly

workflows.name: paired_dge_dgs_ora_workflow
workflows.intent: Run a paired differential gene expression and differential gene splicing analysis from transcript-level counts, aggregate to gene-level, perform over-representation analysis, and visualize the results.
input: counts.csv (transcript-level count matrix with rownames formatted as 'gene:transcript')
metadata.xlsx (sample metadata containing sample IDs and group/condition columns)
workflows.stages:
1. Load the package and define experiment parameters.
2. Run the paired differential expression and splicing analysis using paired_diff.
3. Retrieve gene sets from MSigDB using prepare_msigdb.
4. Run over-representation analysis using paired_ora.
5. Visualize the enrichment scores using plot_ora.
workflows.code:
library("pairedGSEA")

# Defining plotting theme
ggplot2::theme_set(ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 20))

## Load data
# In this vignette we will use the included example Summarized Experiment.
# See ?example_se for more information about the data.
data("example_se") 

if(FALSE){ # Examples of other data imports
    # Example of count matrix
    tx_count <- read.csv("path/to/counts.csv") # Or other load function
    md_file <- "path/to/metadata.xlsx" # Can also be a .csv file or a data.frame
    
    # Example of locally stored DESeqDataSet
    dds <- readRDS("path/to/dds.RDS")
    
    # Example of locally stored SummarizedExperiment
    se <- readRDS("path/to/se.RDS")
}

## Experiment parameters
group_col <- "group_nr" # Column with the groups you would like to compare
sample_col <- "id" # Name of column that specifies the sample id of each sample.
# This is used to ensure the metadata and count data contains the same samples
# and to arrange the data according to the metadata
# (important for underlying tools)
baseline <- 1 # Name of baseline group
case <- 2 # Name of case group
experiment_title <- "TGFb treatment for 12h" # Name of your experiment. This is
# used in the file names that are stored if store_results is TRUE (recommended)

# Check if parameters above fit with metadaata
SummarizedExperiment::colData(example_se)

# Check that all data samples are in the metadata
all(colnames(example_se) %in%
        SummarizedExperiment::colData(example_se)[[sample_col]])

set.seed(500) # For reproducible results

diff_results <- paired_diff(
    object = example_se,
    metadata = NULL, # Use with count matrix or if you want to change it in
    # the input object
    group_col = group_col,
    sample_col = sample_col,
    baseline = baseline,
    case = case,
    experiment_title = experiment_title,
    store_results = FALSE # Set to TRUE (recommended)  if you want
    # to store intermediate results, such as the results on transcript level 
    )

# Define gene sets in your preferred way
gene_sets <- pairedGSEA::prepare_msigdb(
    species = "Homo sapiens", 
    collection = "C5", 
    gene_id_type = "ensembl_gene"
    )

ora <- paired_ora(
    paired_diff_result = diff_results,
    gene_sets = gene_sets,
    experiment_title = NULL # experiment_title - if not NULL,
    # the results will be stored in an RDS object in the 'results' folder
    )

# Scatter plot function with default settings
plot_ora(
    ora,
    paired = FALSE,
    plotly = FALSE,
    pattern = "Telomer", # Identify all gene sets about telomeres
    cutoff = 0.05, # Only include significant gene sets
    lines = TRUE # Guide lines
    )
